# Lisbon Family Trip Snapshot

A relaxed 4-day Lisbon plan for **2 adults + 1 child (age 8)** from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13**, keeping the trip within **€1,800 total excluding flights**. I’ve balanced one **museum day**, one **outdoor day**, and one **food-focused day**, with easy transit and low-stress pacing.

# 4-Day Lisbon Itinerary With Costs

| Day | Focus | Plan | Est. Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 — Apr 10 | Easy arrival + old-town stroll | Baixa/Chiado check-in, elevator or tram ride, riverside sunset, casual dinner | €180–€260 |
| Day 2 — Apr 11 | Museum day | Calouste Gulbenkian Museum, park time, coffee break, early family dinner | €140–€220 |
Media: Alt=| Day 2 — Apr 11 | Museum day | Calouste Gulbenkian Museum, park time, coffee break, early family dinner | €140–€220 |, Lisbon, Portugal
| Day 3 — Apr 12 | Outdoor day | Belém gardens, riverfront walk, Tower/Monument area, pastel de nata stop | €170–€280 |
| Day 4 — Apr 13 | Food-focused day | Market lunch, neighborhood tasting stops, relaxed final dinner, departure buffer | €160–€260 |

## Day-by-Day Family Plan

### Day 1: Easy Arrival in Baixa and Chiado
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and keep the first hours light. If energy is good, walk through **Baixa** and **Rossio**.
- **Afternoon:** Ride the **Santa Justa area** or a short tram segment, then pause in **Chiado** for a snack and playground break.
- **Food:** Simple Portuguese dinner near Chiado or Bairro Alto edge; aim for a place with quick service and kid-friendly options.
- **Estimated cost:** €180–€260 for local transport, snacks, and dinner.
- **Stay neighborhood:** **Baixa/Chiado** for the easiest first-day orientation and walkability.

### Day 2: Museum Day at Gulbenkian
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- **Morning:** Visit the **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** for a calm, high-quality museum experience that works well for adults and an 8-year-old if you keep it to a few highlights.
- **Afternoon:** Relax in the **Gulbenkian Garden**; let your child reset outdoors after the museum.
- **Food:** Lunch nearby, then an early dinner in **Saldanha** or **Avenidas Novas** for an easy return.
- **Estimated cost:** €140–€220 including tickets, lunch, metro/taxi, and dinner.
- **Stay neighborhood:** **Avenidas Novas / Saldanha** for quieter evenings and good transit.

### Day 3: Outdoor Day in Belém
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **Belém** early for the **riverfront**, **Jardim da Praça do Império**, and a gentle walk around the monuments.
- **Afternoon:** Choose one main sight, either **Belém Tower** or the **Monument to the Discoveries**, then spend the rest of the time outdoors.
- **Food:** Family treat stop for **pastéis de nata** and a relaxed lunch in Belém.
- **Estimated cost:** €170–€280 including transit, entry fees if you choose a monument, lunch, and snacks.
- **Stay neighborhood:** **Belém** if you want calmer evenings, or stay central and use tram/train/taxi for the day.

### Day 4: Food-Focused Lisbon
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Morning:** Keep it slow with a café breakfast and a neighborhood wander in **Alfama** or **Mouraria**.
- **Afternoon:** Plan a food-centered lunch stop, then an easy tasting route: pastries, savory bites, and a final gelato or custard stop.
- **Food:** Make this your main culinary day; choose one sit-down lunch and one casual dinner rather than too many stops.
- **Estimated cost:** €160–€260 including meals, coffee, and local transport.
- **Stay neighborhood:** **Alfama / Baixa** if you want atmosphere; **Avenidas Novas** if you prefer easier logistics.

# Best Neighborhoods for a Family Stay

| Neighborhood | Best For | Family Fit | Transit Ease | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baixa/Chiado | First-time visitors, walkability | Very good | Excellent | Best all-around base for a short trip |
| Avenidas Novas/Saldanha | Quiet nights, practical logistics | Excellent | Excellent | Good if you want less noise and easy metro access |
| Belém | Parks, riverfront, slower pace | Good | Good | Best for the outdoor day, less central for daily sightseeing |
| Alfama | Atmosphere and views | Good | Fair | Beautiful, but hills and cobblestones can be tiring with a child |

# Transit Tips For A Relaxed Lisbon Trip

- Use the **metro** for longer cross-city moves; it is the easiest budget-friendly option.
- For a family of 3, **taxis or ride-hailing** can be worth it for uphill or late-evening returns.
- Trams are fun, but don’t rely on them for tight timing; they can be crowded.
- Lisbon’s streets are hilly and often cobbled, so plan shorter walking segments and build in snack breaks.
- If staying central, you can comfortably combine **walking + metro + occasional taxi** and avoid overplanning.

# Spring Packing Checklist

- Light jacket or rain shell
- Layered tops for cool mornings and warmer afternoons
- Comfortable walking shoes with grip
- Compact umbrella
- Sunglasses and sunscreen
- Small daypack
- Reusable water bottles
- Child snacks for transit and museum time
- Power bank and charging cables
- Any motion-sickness remedies if your child is sensitive on trams or hills
- A foldable tote for snacks, souvenirs, or an extra layer

# Budget Fit and Practical Notes

- **Target total excluding flights:** about **€650–€1,020** for 4 days of lodging, food, transit, and admissions if you book sensibly.
- That leaves room for a nicer apartment or a few extra treats while staying under **€1,800** comfortably.
- For the best balance, choose a **2-bedroom apartment or family room in Baixa/Chiado or Avenidas Novas** and keep one main paid activity per day.

# Useful Sources

- Visit Lisboa official tourism: https://www.visitlisboa.com/
- Calouste Gulbenkian Museum: https://gulbenkian.pt/museu/
- Carris public transport: https://www.carris.pt/
- Metro de Lisboa: https://www.metrolisboa.pt/
